scope: Reuse one existing native RSVP producer carrier. No package/fabric baseline, mutation population, product edit, harness edit, build, or runtime validation was performed by this preparation worker.

selected_carrier.reason: This existing carrier already launches three complete Ze daemons and crosses configuration, raw RSVP, native forwarding acknowledgement, installed netlink state and packet delivery. Its scenarios are one top-level test, so the smallest unchanged selection includes its existing FRR cases.
selected_carrier.observer: TestRSVPNativeProducerObserver is invoked by each daemon as an external read-only SDK plugin. rsvpProducerObserve subscribes to lsp-up and reads AF_INET/AF_MPLS routes; it never accepts or installs FIB entries.
selected_carrier.config_source: rsvpProducerNode.configuration, rsvpProducerTunnel and rsvpProducerBypass produce all configs. No parallel configuration set is needed.

requirements.namespace_setup: newRSVPProducerLab configures forwarding, rp_filter, MPLS platform_labels and MPLS input inside private namespaces. The resulting proof does not cover product-driven interface/sysctl provisioning.
requirements.kernel_boundary: The native action checks the booted release against internal/appliance/kernel.version when kernel is supplied. The wrapper also records uname. A capability skip, a host-only run, or an Alpine-default kernel run leaves the shipping-kernel question unverified.

production_chain: cmd/ze/ze_core_start.go: cmdStart explicit-file mode -> hub.Run with bound config source

internal/plugins/rsvpte/register.go: registerRSVPTE declares fib-kernel/sysctl dependencies and runRSVPTEEngine; OnStarted constructs the production raw transport and busFIB; OnConfigApply calls reconcileTunnels
internal/plugins/rsvpte/engine.go: handlePathEgress installs programPop before emitting RESV and Up
internal/plugins/rsvpte/reservation.go: acceptReservation calls installReservation before RESV/Up; installReservation selects swap or push
internal/core/mplsfib/events.go: Apply rejects absent native acknowledgement and propagates owner errors
internal/plugins/fib/kernel/mplsentry_linux.go: netlinkBackend.addMPLSSwap installs AF_MPLS routes, including pop through loopback

assertions.name: native-owner-refusal
assertions.success: An occupied native egress label causes PathErr for tunnel 91; after repeated PATH refresh, no daemon reports Up, no observer records Up, no RESV is captured, and the foreign protocol-100 label remains.
assertions.failure: Any Up/RESV after the refused install or replacement of the foreign label.

assertions.name: installed-state-at-up
assertions.success: Observer snapshots contain the owner-protocol route at each asserted Up: ingress FEC, table and outgoing label; transit/egress matching nonzero incoming label. Bypass lookups return the expected private table-selected label stack and output device, with the carrier's MTU assertion.
assertions.failure: Up without an installed route, plain-IP push lookup, wrong labels/device, or rejected MTU assertion.

assertions.name: actual-forwarding
assertions.success: Fresh dynamically allocated destination sockets receive the exact payload and unchanged ingress IP source. Inbound AF_PACKET capture on M observes the same payload, negotiated label stack and selected link destination MAC. Cases include loose-native, primary-native, context-a, context-b and repaired-native.
assertions.failure: Receive timeout, wrong payload/source/labels/MAC, capture failure, or missing inbound frame. Mere socket send success is insufficient.

assertions.name: withdrawal-and-surviving-forwarding
assertions.success: SIGHUP removal produces the protected PathTear; removing bypass a leaves b delivering b-survives-reload. Sending through removed a returns ENETUNREACH and its payload never appears on the capture, while an unmarked positive-control payload reaches the same destination/link. After daemon shutdown both former context marks are blocked and unmarked forwarding still works.
assertions.failure: Withdrawn context sends successfully, its payload escapes through ordinary routing, surviving b stops delivering, or the positive control fails.

durable_outputs.producer.log: Exact selected carrier output including PASS/FAIL/SKIP and failure daemon logs.
durable_outputs.network.trace: strace follows the test and its children and records network syscalls without fault injection. Retains netlink route replies, AF_PACKET frame receives, successful UDP receives and withdrawal ENETUNREACH errors before carrier cleanup.
durable_outputs.invocation.json: Exact executed argv, kernel release, input executable hashes and source snapshot hashes.
durable_outputs.sources/: Copies of assertion and producer sources used to interpret the trace; Main must establish that binaries match them.
durable_outputs.result.json: Carrier status based on exact test PASS, process exit, absence of test SKIP and a nonempty trace. It does not independently decode captured bytes or establish foreign interoperability.
durable_outputs.ip-version.txt: iproute2 version used by namespace launch.

pass_policy: Accept kernel evidence only after the selected carrier executes all its assertions without skip/failure, its binary provenance matches the saved source, the native host action confirms the selected runtime kernel and durable trace/log files exist. A prepared driver, successful compilation, nonempty trace, or exit zero with SKIP is insufficient.

other_existing_carriers.boundary: Production raw transport and Linux namespace packet carriage, with hand-built signaling state. Useful diagnostics but no full daemon producer acceptance proof on their own. Do not repeat for this preparation.
Kernel MPLS entries and frame forwarding driven directly at the FIB boundary; does not establish RSVP producer coupling.

other_existing_carriers.source: internal/le/qemu/alltests.go: vmSuites and integration package population; internal/le/qemu/guestlabs.go: netnsSuiteNames
other_existing_carriers.boundary: all-tests includes rsvpte; qemu netns-test targets firewall/policy/ospf/ospfv3/pppoe and has no RSVP selector. Use qemu run with the precise carrier instead of all-tests or an invented RSVP action.
Single-daemon configuration and show coverage; no peer or labeled end-to-end forwarding proof.

foreign_peer.evidence: Case-insensitive searches for RSVP, rsvpd, rsvpte and rsvp-te returned no matching lab configuration in these roots. Interop lab directories cover BGP, IPsec, PPPoE, L2TP and RADIUS. test/rsvpte/rsvpte-lsp-setup.ci explicitly describes its missing live RSVP peer.
foreign_peer.scope: This establishes absence from the inspected repository labs, not absence of possible external implementations or owner-managed equipment.
foreign_peer.required_before_claim: A named independent RSVP implementation/version, accessible image or device, runnable configuration, compatible protocol/topology and captured PATH/RESV plus labeled packet/withdrawal evidence.
foreign_peer.kernel_independence: Ze-to-Ze is sufficient to attempt the native producer/kernel coupling question. It cannot be reported as foreign or cross-vendor RSVP interoperability.

bounded_limitations: No runtime result is claimed, and the driver was not executed or syntax-checked under this preparation-only assignment.
The unchanged carrier also depends on native OSPF adjacency/identity, SSH readiness and config reload; failures there block this execution rather than prove an RSVP kernel defect.

The carrier checks kernel-route snapshots when its asynchronous Up observer handles the event; it does not timestamp netlink installation against the instant the producer publishes the event. Source sequencing and the real EEXIST negative case support the acceptance-order boundary.

Normal tunnel removal asserts session disappearance and protected PathTear; the discriminating post-withdrawal packet check is for private bypass contexts. Do not expand it into proof that every downstream AF_MPLS label is absent after all ordinary withdrawals.
The carrier validates end-to-end delivery and incoming label stacks at M; it does not assert a standalone captured swap label on every transit link.
strace adds observation overhead. A timeout remains a failed or incomplete attempt; do not turn it into a pass. Preserve the trace to distinguish readiness, timeout and dataplane assertions.
The carrier has an explicit native-push MTU assertion. Failure of that assertion must be inspected against current producer/kernel semantics, without weakening it merely to obtain a pass.
RESV_CONFIRM is requested by augmenting a genuinely captured reservation; this injected request does not constitute a foreign-peer implementation.
The already-passed package/fabric baseline and 25 selected mutation claims are intentionally outside this execution.
